name: Podere Sapaio Sapaio 2016
text:
## Podere Sapaio Sapaio 2016

**The story.** Podere Sapaio is a [Bolgheri](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Podere+Sapaio,+Castagneto+Carducci,+Italy&t=k) estate on Tuscany's Etruscan Coast, founded when Massimo Piccin bought land at Lo Scopaio in 1999; since 2004 it has made two Bordeaux-style reds, Sapaio and Volpolo. The vineyards lie near the sea, swept by maritime winds, on alluvial soils that suit [Bordeaux varieties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordeaux_wine) ([Bottle of Italy](https://bottleofitaly.com/en/pages/cantine-podere-sapio)). The celebrated consultant Carlo Ferrini makes the wines, and Decanter has said Sapaio has been "shaping a cult following" since 1999 ([Wine Access](https://www.wineaccess.com/catalog/2016-podere-sapaio-toscana_31b03644-1e34-47db-8b96-566df703c499)).

**The wine.** The 2016 is a blend of [Cabernet Sauvignon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabernet_Sauvignon), [Cabernet Franc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabernet_Franc) and [Petit Verdot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petit_Verdot). The Wine Advocate explains that much of the 2016's fruit came from vineyards in [Bibbona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bibbona), just outside the Bolgheri appellation, so it is labelled Toscana IGT; about 20,000 bottles were made ([Wine Access](https://www.wineaccess.com/catalog/2016-podere-sapaio-toscana_31b03644-1e34-47db-8b96-566df703c499)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Tuscany vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/tuscany) calls 2016 another good vintage, with deep colour and impressive fragrance, though yields were down by up to a fifth.

**What the critics say for 2016.** As quoted by [Wine Access](https://www.wineaccess.com/catalog/2016-podere-sapaio-toscana_31b03644-1e34-47db-8b96-566df703c499):
- **[James Suckling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Suckling): 96**. "So vivid and polished on the nose", blackcurrant, blueberry and lavender; full-bodied, with firm, very silky tannins and a long finish. "Needs two or three years to start coming together, but already gorgeous to taste."
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 95**. Dark chocolate and spice balanced by rich, sweet fruit; blackberry, plum and dark currant; "well-balanced, fragrant and absolutely seamless".
- **Wine Access** (merchant's note). Herbes de Provence, tomato leaf and wild raspberries; generous, with stamina and pleasant acidity. Now to 2030.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 91.9** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is ten years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2019 to 2035. So it is in its prime: cassis, blueberry, herbs and chocolate. Decant one to two hours ahead and serve at 17°C.

**Food.** Bolgheri reds love grilled and roast meat: Tuscan [bistecca alla fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bistecca_alla_fiorentina), wild boar stew, roast lamb with rosemary, or aged Pecorino.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Sapaio at the moment.

**Curious details**
- **Outside the line.** In 2016 Sapaio wore a humbler Toscana IGT label simply because much of its fruit grew just over the Bolgheri boundary, in Bibbona ([Wine Access](https://www.wineaccess.com/catalog/2016-podere-sapaio-toscana_31b03644-1e34-47db-8b96-566df703c499)).
